_meta.note: Phase x domain matrix underpinning Table 2 of the manuscript. Items are prompts for clinical judgement, not mandatory protocols.

phases.pre_tournament: 6-12 months before (club-country data sharing; baseline assessment)

cardiovascular.label: Cardiovascular
pre_tournament: Health questionnaire, examination and 12-lead ECG with sex-appropriate interpretation; echocardiography where indicated
Confirm emergency action plan and AED access for training venues
preparation_camp: Review outstanding cardiac investigations; confirm eligibility
in_tournament: Post-viral illness cardiac red flags before return to play
post_tournament: Share findings with club medical team (with consent)

musculoskeletal.label: Musculoskeletal (ACL, hamstring, ankle)
pre_tournament: Injury history and ACL/hamstring risk profile
Audit neuromuscular training adherence (>=10 min, 2x/week)
Strength and hop/change-of-direction testing
preparation_camp: Maintain neuromuscular programme; progressive exposure to match-intensity running
in_tournament: Daily medical screening; minutes and high-intensity load; on-field assessment readiness
post_tournament: Report time-loss injuries using football consensus definitions; handover

energy_iron.label: Energy availability and iron status
pre_tournament: REDs screening (IOC REDs CAT2) and dietary assessment
Ferritin, haemoglobin and iron indices; plan supplementation early
preparation_camp: Individual fuelling plans for heat, travel and congested fixtures
in_tournament: Body-mass trends; time any blood sampling away from recent exercise (hepcidin peaks 3-6 h)
post_tournament: Repeat iron indices if deficient; refer as needed

menstrual_female_health.label: Menstrual cycle and female health domains
pre_tournament: Menstrual history, contraception use, symptoms; breast and pelvic-floor health (female health domains)
Agree consent and data-governance for cycle tracking
preparation_camp: Individual symptom-management plans; product and facility access
in_tournament: Optional cycle-phase and symptom logging; interpret load and fatigue in context
post_tournament: Record female health problems using the IOC supplement taxonomy

heat_environment.label: Heat, cold and environment
pre_tournament: Map fixtures and base camp to venue climate (Table 1); identify heat-exposed players
Heat-tolerance history, including previous exertional heat illness
preparation_camp: Heat acclimation 1-2 weeks if north-east fixtures; cold/wet routines for southern venues
Individual cooling plan (ice slurry, ice vest)
in_tournament: On-site WBGT; hydration and body-mass checks; account for higher luteal-phase core temperature

infection_vaccination.label: Infection and vaccination
pre_tournament: Vaccination review: yellow fever (state-dependent), influenza, measles, COVID-19; consider dengue vaccination per national guidance
Travel-health consultation
preparation_camp: Hand and respiratory hygiene; food and water safety; mosquito-bite prevention
in_tournament: Daily illness symptom check; isolation protocol; outbreak bulletins for host cities
post_tournament: Screen for febrile illness after return (arboviral incubation)

mental_health.label: Mental health
pre_tournament: Validated mental-health screening; referral pathways
preparation_camp: Agree support access in the tournament environment
in_tournament: Brief check-ins; attention to selection, media and social-media stressors

concussion.label: Concussion
pre_tournament: Baseline concussion assessment; education for players and coaches
preparation_camp: Rehearse on-field recognition and removal; clarify medical authority
in_tournament: Apply protocol free from player/coach pressure; video review where available

travel_sleep.label: Travel, jet lag and sleep
pre_tournament: Plan arrival timing (European teams cross 4-5 time zones; Asia-Pacific teams many more)
preparation_camp: Light, sleep and meal-timing strategies; arrive early enough to adapt
in_tournament: Minimise domestic travel fatigue (distances up to ~3200 km); sleep monitoring

medication.label: Medication and anti-doping
pre_tournament: Medication reconciliation; therapeutic use exemptions
in_tournament: Log all medication; avoid routine pre-match NSAIDs

respiratory_airway.label: Airway health, asthma/EIB and air quality
pre_tournament: Screen for asthma and exercise-induced bronchoconstriction with objective testing (exercise challenge or eucapnic voluntary hyperpnoea), not symptoms alone
Record treatment plans; check inhaled doses against the current anti-doping limits and whether a therapeutic use exemption is needed
Review venue air-quality context and identify athletes who need it watched
preparation_camp: Stock reliever and preventer inhalers plus spares and spacers for every venue
Set session rules for elevated pollution days (timing away from peak traffic, indoor alternatives)
Extended warm-up routine for athletes with EIB
in_tournament: Check local air quality before outdoor sessions; apply the planning bands
Check symptoms before and after training in athletes with airway disease; watch cold, damp venues as well as polluted ones
Record any inhaled medication with the rest of the medication log
post_tournament: Review airway symptoms and treatment; refer for reassessment if control was poor
